legend.title: June to August trend · kg/m² per decade

caption: NASA AIRS (Aqua satellite) TotH2OVap · 2003–2025 · Sen's slope of the June to August mean of each year in each 2° square. Strong colour: passes the map-wide test for false alarms (Mann-Kendall with memory correction, q = 0.05). This map enlarges areas near the poles.

processing: one OPeNDAP DAP4 subset per monthly granule: SurfAirTemp_A, SurfAirTemp_D, TotH2OVap_A, TotH2OVap_D (no other fields)
day/night mean = (ascending ~1:30 pm + descending ~1:30 am) / 2, only where both orbits have a value (3411 native cell-months with a single orbit were left out)
mean of June to August in each year 2003–2025 (December counts towards the next year) in each 2° square
per-square Sen's slope and Mann-Kendall (Yue-Wang), BH FDR across squares (trend_stats.py)
provenance.caveat: Data: NASA AIRS infrared sounder on the Aqua satellite, 1° squares, average of the ~1:30 am and ~1:30 pm passes; a satellite retrieval, not a weather model (MERRA-2 does use AIRS measurements, so the two are not fully independent) (the map averages them into 2° squares). The trend is a straight line through 2003–2025; it shows what changed, not why. The record is 23 years long, shorter than the 30 years usually used to describe a climate. AIRS sees mostly clear and partly cloudy skies, and its global water-vapour trend is much smaller than MERRA-2's (about +0.1 vs +0.5 kg/m² per decade, 2003–2025); treat this trend as not yet confirmed.
